scope_statement: THIS FILE CONTAINS NO STATEMENT ABOUT HQC.  Every value is an exact moment of a TOY, ENUMERABLE ensemble defined in oracle.py.  No configuration here is HQC's error distribution, no configuration here uses HQC's inner or outer code, and nothing here asserts that assumption A17 does or does not hold, or that HQC's decoding-failure-rate model is or is not correct.  Claim tier: toy.  certificate.kind: none (no solve and no relation is claimed).  The oracle is a CORRECTNESS INSTRUMENT for a later estimator, not a research result.

convention.C1_distinct_indices: mu_k(J) = E[prod_{j in J} F_j] over DISTINCT block indices J; repetition is forbidden because F_j^2 = F_j makes a repeated index collapse onto a lower-order moment (an over-estimate).
convention.C2_canonical_scalar: mu_k = (1/C(n_e,k)) sum_{|J|=k} mu_k(J) = E[C(S,k)]/C(n_e,k), the normalised k-th binomial moment of S = sum_j F_j.  The full per-subset table is reported alongside it whenever it is enumerable, and subset-exchangeability is TESTED, not assumed.
convention.C3_unconditional: No conditioning on the global weight of etilde, on S, or on anything else.
convention.C4_tie_breaking: Where the inner ML decoder ties, F_j is Bernoulli with an exact rational parameter given the block content, with tie-breaking independent across blocks (rider R-tie).
convention.blocks: B_j = {j*n_2, ..., (j+1)*n_2 - 1}, disjoint and consecutive, per TASK-20260802-15971b section 1.
convention.m: m = delta_e + 1, the smallest number of symbol errors that defeats the outer decoder.  Set explicitly per configuration.

randomness_sources.used_for: the i.i.d. NULL GENERATOR sampler and the Monte-Carlo self-test ONLY
randomness_sources.not_used_for: any exact computation; every mu_k, tail, variance and reference value is deterministic exact arithmetic

floating_point_used_for: the standard error / z-score of the Monte-Carlo self-test

configurations.role: I.I.D. NULL (duty 3): independent by construction at the coordinate level
I.I.D. NULL with rational per-block failure probability (tie splitting)
KNOWN-ANSWER NEGATIVE DEPENDENCE with an INDEPENDENT closed form (inclusion-exclusion over empty blocks)
KNOWN-ANSWER POSITIVE DEPENDENCE (duty 4): a latent mixture over a common parameter, strict by Jensen for k>=2

BOTH MECHANISMS IN ONE OBJECT: each component is negatively dependent (sampling without replacement); the mixture over the latent global weight is positively dependent.  This is the shape EV-HQC-6fd5b1 O-6 describes; it is a property of THIS TOY, not of HQC.
KNOWN-ANSWER extreme positive dependence (mu_k = p for all k)
I.I.D. NULL at the indicator level (duty 3, second construction)
HQC-SHAPED RING ENSEMBLE on space (T), n prime > n_e*n_2 so 1 coordinate is truncated (assumption A23's shape)

ring_symmetry_check.note: Block shift equivariance is a DERIVATION (the law of e' = x*r2 + r1*y + e is invariant under cyclic shift of F_2^n because the fixed-weight sets are shift-invariant and ring multiplication commutes with shift, and B_{j+1} is the translate of B_j by n_2), and it is VERIFIED here rather than assumed.  FULL subset exchangeability is NOT implied by it: when n = n_e*n_2 the group acting is only the CYCLIC group of order n_e, so mu_k(J) is constant on cyclic orbits of k-subsets and may differ BETWEEN orbits. That is what is observed at k = 2 (adjacent vs opposite block pairs).  This is a property of THESE TOY CONFIGURATIONS and is not a statement about HQC.

sampler_vs_oracle_check.purpose: Does the oracle's exact mu_m equal what a SAMPLING estimator of the same ensemble converges to?  This is the check that the oracle certifies the SAME OBJECT an estimator targets.  Toy ring only; NOT the HQC decoding measurement.

M1_indices_with_replacement.description: Draws m block indices WITH REPLACEMENT and averages the product of the indicators: E[(S/n_e)^m].  Because F_j^2 = F_j, every repeated index collapses onto a lower-order moment, so M1 >= truth ALWAYS and the excess is read as positive dependence.  THIS IS THE BUG THAT LOOKS LIKE SIGNAL.

M2_ordered_distinct_wrong_denominator.description: Correctly forbids repeats (ordered distinct m-tuples) but normalises by n_e^m instead of the falling factorial n_e^{(m)}; biased DOWNWARD by the factor n_e^{(m)}/n_e^m.

M3_binomial_count_wrong_denominator.description: Counts m-subsets correctly (C(S,m)) but divides by n_e^m instead of C(n_e,m); biased DOWNWARD by m!.

M4_single_fixed_subset_0..m-1.description: Uses one fixed subset J = {0,...,m-1} instead of averaging over all subsets.  Unbiased iff the failure indicators are subset-exchangeable; biased otherwise.  The ring configurations are where this bites.

monte_carlo_demonstration.purpose: DEMONSTRATION that the oracle discriminates a correct estimator from the over-counting mutant.  This is NOT evidence about anything; it is a self-test of the instrument.

reach_demonstrations.why_not_hqc: The ensemble is UNIFORM FIXED WEIGHT over N coordinates, which is NOT the law of HQC's etilde = x*r2 + r1*y + e; the block decoder is a bounded-distance WEIGHT THRESHOLD at an arbitrarily chosen t, which is NOT HQC's duplicated Reed-Muller ML decoder.  Only the DIMENSIONS are HQC-1-shaped.  This number is a demonstration of computational reach and is not comparable to any published DFR.

estimator_sample_size_requirements.what_this_is: Exact per-sample variance of the canonical estimator C(S,m)/C(n_e,m) when S ~ Binomial(n_e, p) -- i.e. under the i.i.d. null -- and the exact sample count T needed for a target relative standard error.  n_e and m are free parameters and p is swept over hypothetical values.  NO HQC MARGINAL IS ASSERTED OR USED; this is a property of the estimator, provided as input to a feasibility analysis.
